Uniform Title: Kulānandādi Manuscript: NGMCP 1-1376/v Reel Number: A40/6

Description: The manuscript titled *Kulānandādi* contains short tracts and fragments of early Kaula works. The first, entitled *Kulānanda*, occupies the initial seven folios. Although brief, it is significant as it is attributed to Matsyendranātha. It addresses various aspects of Kaula Yoga, primarily focusing on the "piercing" (*vedha*) of the channels of the subtle body by means of spiritual energy descending from above, as well as the upward piercing of *kuṇḍalinī*. The style and structure of its exposition, consistent with other Kaula tracts attributed to Matsyendranātha, supports the view that this is indeed an early Kaula text. The subsequent four folios treat the characteristics of the *kapāla* (skull-cup), which is said to be derived from the *Picumata* (i.e., the *Brahmayāmala*); this attribution is plausible, as that text does indeed address this subject. The remainder of the manuscript contains prescriptions for Kaula ritual. The deities mentioned belong to an early period, including Kubjikā, *Kālasaṃkarṣiṇī*, *Bhagamālinī*, and others. Notably, *Tripurā* is absent, though one of her precursors, *Kāmeśvarī*, is present.
Notes: In the manuscript, *anusvāra* and *visarga* occur together.

Oṃ, homage to Bhairava!
The goddess Umā questioned the God of gods, the teacher of the world, who was seated upon the peak of Kailāsa, regarding the supreme knowledge in its entirety.
O Supreme One, bringer of joy to the Kula, tell us how that which is without division yet appears divided is established within the body, and describe that primordial non-duality.

Tell me, according to the specific locations of the vital points (*sthāna*), how consciousness (*vijñāna*) is established within the body; [tell me of] those *jaya*-channels which produce immediate conviction.
The paralyzing of fetters, the entering [of others' bodies], the shaking, and likewise the trembling;
the simultaneous entry with dogs, the collective entry, and the manifestation of divine speech.
The sequence for overcoming hatred from afar, as well as the great pervasion (*mahāvyāpti*),
the sky-farer (*khecara*), the state of equal flavor (*samarasa*), and the destroyer of strength and graying hair.
"O Lord of the Gods, O Master, tell me everything.
Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the most excellent *Pūrabheda*.
This is the Kaulika knowledge, the eighth [chapter] in the *Kulānanda*.
In the station of Brahmā is a lotus endowed with sixty-four petals.
Having mentally projected it right there, the practitioner, with his face turned toward the excellent divine [vision], beholds the marks and the crest of the island within the entire body.
By merely perceiving that, the supreme accomplishment is born;
it is located above the navel, within the lotus, according to the wise.
There the god Bhairava, the lord of the universe, stands facing him;
having mentally placed [the deity] before him, with his intention firmly resolved.
There, through the specific sounds of the winds, the genus (jāti) is born;
by the mere knowledge of this, one certainly effects possession (āveśa).
2a) One is born into the supreme state; there is no need for deliberation on this matter.
Now, O Goddess, another supreme [method] which produces immediate conviction:
I shall explain that to you, O Goddess; listen, O lady with long eyes, to the second limb which has been described by me as being thus.
If one fixes the mind on that very point, what has been taught will certainly arise:
the past, the future, and likewise the present.
Right there, one whose form is like intense light should project the creation;
having pierced the lotus situated in the heart, it should fill the aperture at the crown of the head.
In this way, one effects the paralysis of the fetters if the mind rests;
then, O Goddess, another supreme divine vision proceeds.
One should visualize the "knotted twice-born" (dvijagranthi) situated in the midst of blazing flames; there itself, with the mind restrained, one should honor the four crests (cūlikās).
O Goddess, creation proceeds from the locus; there is no need for deliberation regarding this matter.
The Goddess said:
I have not revealed that piercing of the excellent essence (*sadvasāra*) which is *rohita*;
explain it in detail, so that I may understand its recitation at that very moment.
Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, as I explain the essence of the Vedas in due order: in the station of Brahmā, there is a lotus with sixty petals.
Right there, one should bring forth the creation through the staff-like fiery splendor;
likewise, having pierced the great knot as well as the two wheels.
One should visualize a lotus at the crown of the head, blazing in form;
by causing it to move and whirl, the surface of the great earth is surely set in motion.
It pierces mountains and trees; how much more so small creatures?
Now, O Goddess, listen to another supreme, auspicious knowledge.
One should contemplate the black earth situated between the eyebrows and the eyes.
The left stream, possessing exceedingly intense brilliance and radiance,
flows constantly until it reaches the head of the Cakravartin.
One should contemplate the consciousness of this [being], which is difficult to hear, as it possesses the true cause;
indeed, until that [consciousness] on the left side becomes intensely radiant with light.
The Goddess said:
The destruction of wrinkles and grey hair has been described by you as "divine beauty" before me;
O Lord, tell me this, for I have a doubt regarding it, O God.
Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall declare that which is difficult even for the gods to obtain:
a thirty-two-petaled lotus stands upon his head, situated in the center.
Right there, one should meditate upon the nectar endowed with the sixteen digits;
one should cause it to fall through the heart-cakra down to the circle of the navel.
One should contemplate the entire city as being of black color and subject to disintegration; O Goddess of excellent vows, one may arrest premature graying in a single month.
Then, O Goddess, there is another supreme state, a station of pure doubt;
where there is a crossroads, there is the abode of all the Asuras.
There he established his mind as the divine speech proceeded;
the one with the divine, excellent countenance spoke words never heard before, and he spoke those words.
It effects the withdrawal of the objects of the senses for the destruction of fever and disease;
beyond that is the supreme state, wherein all things proceed.
Then, O Goddess, I shall describe another supreme [method] which is difficult to penetrate:
situated in the midst of a blazing fire, one perceives right there two [lines] marked by a cross, possessing a radiance equal to ten million suns.
4a) Having caused the upward-pointing power (ūrddhaśakti) to descend, the wise one should pierce [the center];
having pierced it, he should then observe that [target].

Having fashioned a spear from wood blazing with fire, one should whirl it like a wheel; then, one should pierce through armor and shields that are as solid as mountains—what need is there to mention those that are merely equal to them?
"Knowing this, O beautiful lady, the practitioner who moves about at will becomes difficult for gods, asuras, and humans to find. The Goddess said:
O Goddess, regarding the trembling of the bows as it was described before me, there remains a doubt; therefore, O Lord, tell me about it, O Master.
Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall explain the shaking, the trembling, and the state of being established:
that great-carrying channel (nāḍī) which exists in the form of a coiled serpent (kuṇḍalī).
Right there, one should fix the gaze with great luster in the shape of a staff upon the son.
In the heart-cakra, O Goddess, the deities possess the excellent forms of intense power;
there is shaking and trembling, and no deliberation regarding the task is required here.
Now, O Goddess, hear of another supreme state of sky-faring (*khecaratva*), O Beloved; those [channels] which, like the shape of the *kuṇḍalī*, are situated in succession.

In the two feet is the Great Seat; again, the lotus situated on the crown should be made to blaze like fire. One should cause it to expand through the power of penetration (*vedha*) from the center with all one's might. From that penetration of the sky-farer (*khecara*), one shall receive the unprecedented bliss for nine days.
5a) Now, O fair-faced one, I shall further explain the great pervasion (mahāvyāpti),
as it is known by me to exist within the locations of fire (vahni).
In the same way, having fixed the mind upon the tip of the nose while conceiving oneself as the wind,
the wise one, having pierced that mind, should unite it with the partless (niṣkala).
O Goddess, if one were to speak a falsehood regarding your great pervasiveness (*mahāvyāpti*),
then I shall explain another method by which success (*siddhi*) will certainly be attained.
O observer of good vows, having taken the second [letter] from the group that transcends the classes in direct order,
and having placed it upon the fire (R), one should join it with the fourth vowel.
First, the wise one should join the [seed-syllable] pierced at its head by the Bindu;
then again, O Goddess, that which transcends the groups (vargātīta), adorned with the sixth vowel.
O Goddess, one should again join that which is marked with the name of the crescent-moon and the bindu;
having taken the fifth [vowel] of the letter *ya*, it should be endowed with the third vowel.
One should cause the burden, joined with the second [house], to be performed by the beloved sons.
One should employ the first seed-syllable of the group as the primordial creation;
O Goddess, this is declared to be the Kula, endowed with the Vidyā.
But one should always, O Goddess, apply the mind with single-pointed concentration;
for him, O beautiful one, all success in all branches of knowledge shall come to pass.
O Goddess with the face of Saṃvara, even if one’s own mind were exhausted by this,
there is yet another supreme [practice] that causes one to be overwhelmed by desire.
Seated in the middle of the *bhaga*, at midday within the *bhaga*,
the wind is impelled by the *śakti* and takes the form of a blazing fire through its splendor.
O Goddess, one should contemplate poison as a lotus upon the head of the fearful;
O Yoginī, one should contemplate nectar and radiant energy through the path of the ears.
Even women of noble lineage, O Goddess, become observers of excellent vows in a single moment;
furthermore, O Goddess, there is another supreme [practice], namely the drawing forth of fruits and flowers.
Listen, O Goddess supreme in descent, whose primordial prowess is formidable:
the wise one should draw in the wind; the form residing in the *piṇḍa* is not pleasing to the taste.
O Goddess, at that very moment one should employ fruit and flower;
one should contemplate them as being composed of radiant threads, well-strung together.
The Goddess said:
O Lord, I have indeed proclaimed ignorance everywhere regarding those devoted to that [path];
even now, O Goddess, there remains a doubt—tell me, what is it, O Master?
The end of doubt is caused by destruction.
Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim that which is difficult even for the gods to obtain:
having made the seat firm, one gazes upon the universe without turning back.
O Goddess, I meditate upon non-existence, which is devoid of all existence.
Having made the consciousness steady upon that reality, one should fix it in the center of space;
O Goddess, the wise one should contemplate the equality of essence between the master and the servant.
This is proclaimed there as being merely consciousness in the middle;
the piercing-stob is at the beginning, consisting of consciousness that is difficult to hear.
Possession, biting, scratching, trembling, and likewise paralysis—
these occur for the yogin through the power of another; by practicing that, O one of noble vows, [he attains mastery].
Thus ends the *Kulānanda*, which is the descent of the feet of Matsyendra.
May there be well-being for the entire world.
I bow at the feet of him by whom I was initiated by my own guru— the guru of Yonātha, who [was the disciple] of Ādinātha.
7b) Thus it has been stated,
O beautiful one, according to reality.
Thus ends the description of the skull according to the Picumata.
And he said to Nañca.
Whether it be produced from an anthill, or even if it is defective and devoid of all auspicious marks,
having seen such a vessel turned face upwards, one should break it and then take [another].
The Khecarīmudrā is proclaimed as the refuge of all supernatural powers (siddhis) for those whose face remains fixed and endowed with all the proper characteristics.
If one gives a vessel made of earth, enjoyments arise; if one stands up while giving, however, one should not accept it.
Indeed, that vessel which has its opening facing downward should be characterized by auspicious marks.
The wise man should not accept that which is a source for the attainment of *khecarī*, yet bestows lower accomplishments;
therefore, he should avoid it.
When the practitioner grasps it with his face turned sideways and recites the mantra with even hips, then it shall bestow accomplishment.
The procedure for atonement for the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra, in due order.
O lady of excellent complexion, one who is endowed with these eleven characteristics should have mats made from the materials previously mentioned in the Sūtra for the Mothers.
One should prepare the argha vessel, which bestows all accomplishments;
[now follows] the characteristics of the skull-cup (kapāla).
1a) Oṃ, homage to the gurus beginning with Śiva.
O Goddess, at the time of initiation and likewise during the Great Yoga,
the vessel for the Śakti is indeed shaped like the back of a tortoise.
O lady of excellent complexion, listen as I describe to you the characteristics of those skulls known as the "sixth lotus," which are capable of all [magical] feats:
its back is long and thin, and its front horn becomes prominent.
O Goddess, the skull was placed facing forward; [the remainder] is merely... * * *.
Where the skull is elevated like a fish and perfectly circular,
having a shape resembling the back of a tortoise, that is called *kūrmapṛṣṭha*.
And what is the *vaśaka*? When asked thus, the *rājapṛṣṭha* should be performed.
It is declared by the King that this [back] is endowed with these characteristics:
where the side is elevated and situated in the shape of an elephant's frontal globe (kumbha).
It is described as being depressed in the middle and shaped like an elephant’s frontal globe,
extending from the forehead all the way up to the neck.
From these, the universe arises, and from that, it becomes divided into six parts;
this,
endowed with these characteristics, is declared to be the vessel for the Śakti.
If the lotus on the back is level and situated in a concave depression, that bowl shall be lotus-shaped; it is proclaimed as a "padma" [lotus] bowl.
Their characteristics have been described to you; now hear of their castes—whether Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, or Śūdra, O venerable one, there is no doubt.
These castes are declared for the Vadhvārya, and for the Kapāla as well, there is no doubt.
O woman of excellent complexion, that which has a hollow is seen in its crest.
One, two, three, or four skull-bowls in sequence;
a single aperture is prescribed for a Brahmin, while two apertures are traditionally taught for a Kṣatriya.
A Vaiśya is said to have three apertures, while a Śūdra has four;
that which has five streams and six apertures is proclaimed to be of the nature of an intoxicated man.
Indeed, beginning from the five streams and extending up to twenty,
there are cranial fragments (*kapāla*) in the various births within the cavities.
2a) Those that are flawless, produced by me, and not designated as "skull" (kapāla)—
whatever vessel belongs to the four castes, provided it possesses the [proper] characteristics, that should be accepted.
O Great Goddess, the practitioner should avoid all [women] belonging to the six castes, even if they possess auspicious marks; of this there is no doubt.
One should also avoid a fourth type of bowl that is impure:
one that is dark-colored, as well as short, and likewise has a blackish luster.
One should likewise avoid those that are red in color;
if they are dark-colored, a great disease will arise for the practitioner.
Death occurs if it is black in color; suffering arises if it is red.
The skull should be circular and endowed with all the auspicious marks.
And this has been declared as the foremost; there is no need for deliberation here.
Therefore, even when the characteristic is associated with it, there should be an abandonment of that country.
That which is red-colored belongs to the fire element; it should be cracked on all sides.
It causes distress and generates agitation; one should avoid such inauspicious [cracks].
That which appears as one's own reflection, resembling a conch shell, a jasmine flower, or the moon, is indeed pure.
That vessel which is honey-colored and possesses a glossy luster should be grasped by the foremost of practitioners; it is proclaimed to bestow enjoyment.
That which bestows enjoyment is also proclaimed; it should indeed be accepted by practitioners, resembling cow's butter and likewise possessing a glossy luster.
That which is grasped by the practitioner is declared to be the bestower of enjoyment;
when it is white and flows abundantly, that is proclaimed as liberation.
Thus Bhairava spoke, declaring that it bestows liberation:
"The female skull should be circular, and its thickness should be proportionate to that."
That which has two layers is thus described; it should be taken by practitioners.
It is proclaimed that from that [practice], liberation is to be grasped by those seeking release, and worldly enjoyment is obtained.
3a) Single-layered [seals] are difficult to obtain; however,
O Dear One, those with two layers should also be accepted by means of these characteristics.
A skull-cup that is a single solid piece is difficult to find even for the gods;
therefore, if it remains small, one will not attain the stage of the practice of the Vidyā.
Resembling fresh butter, it may have a cough-like sound and be enclosed within a mound;
it is characterized by concealed veins and is indeed hidden and very firm.
That too is said to be rare, yet it bestows all accomplishments;
the two types, the *dvimaṇḍala* and the *trikhaṇḍa*, are proclaimed as the givers of worldly enjoyment (*bhukti*).
Whether it be five sections, six sections, or likewise seven sections, these may be accepted by one desiring worldly enjoyment; however, for one established in liberation, they are auspicious.

O lady of virtuous vows, that which has come into one's hand shall become a hundred fragments; yet, if one offers it while rising, perfection is attained at that very moment through the consecration by water.

Kārttikeya said:
Having bowed his head to the god Śrīkaṇṭha together with Umā,
Māyā agitates herself, creates the universe, and transforms it.
Salutations to you, who bring supreme bliss to the mind, appearing in the form of a serpent!
Ananta, Vāsukī, Takṣaka, Karkoṭaka, Padma, Mahāpadma, Saṅkhapāla, and Āstīka— these are proclaimed as the eight Nāgas.
Whether one follows the Svacchanda, Vaiṣṇava, Vedic, or even the Matha tradition,
this rite must be performed according to the prescribed rule for Varuṇa.
O King, one should worship the seed-syllable of Maṣṇi there,
having first performed the fire-oblation and other rites according to the rules prescribed in the Vedas.
Having performed her bath, the twilight prayers, and the ritual worship of the deities, the preceptor,
having washed his hands and feet, entered the sacrificial pavilion.
Having assumed the lotus posture (padmāsana), facing either eastward or northward.
Having performed the ritual placement on the limbs (karanyāsa) and so forth, the Guru again offers the water of respect (arghya).
In each respective case, the scripture of Śiva is that which is prescribed by the scriptures declared in the Vedas.
And it was adorned with sacrificial pits, pavilions, banners, and flags.
The lord of mangoes, with mango sprouts, cane leaves, bamboo leaves, and *prakṣa* and *udumbara* fruits;

Next, I shall describe the archways starting from the east: the udumbara, the vaṭa, and the plakṣa.
Thus ends the section on the archway.

And in the intermediate directions, the *devadāru* tree. Thus [is the arrangement] for the gateways located at the cardinal and intermediate points. Next follows the sequence for the banners (*patākā*).
2a) The banners are red like Indra’s bow (the rainbow), black with the luster of the dark-blue moon,
white like a parrot, golden in color, and like crystal.
In the lower portion, however, she is smoke-colored; in the north-west, she has the luster of saffron.
The upper one, however, is white in color. Thus are the ten banners.
Having performed the ritual assignment of limbs (*aṅganyāsa*) with the mantra "Oṃ tat savitur vareṇyam," the Guru prepares the *argha* offering for the *praṇava*.
First, the mantra for the door: the door is consecrated with the weapon-mantra (astra).
One should worship with: *oṃ akṣarāhvāyakitaraḥ*. *Oṃ hrīṃ śusobhakalādvārā namaḥ*.
Above the door.
With the verse "ye te panthāḥ," one should worship each pair of rivers.
Oṃ, salutation to Śubhadra. Oṃ, salutation to Bhadra. Thus for the two branches.
2b) Oṃ, homage to the auspicious archway.
At the archway: Oṃ, obeisance to Kumuda. At the flagpole: [recite] "Oṃ indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan...
and perform the worship of the banner.
Oṃ hrīṃ vajrāya hūṃ phaṭ, homage to the banner.
Having performed the invocation and so forth, and having offered water for the feet, water for sipping, and flowers;
Then, having gone to the southeast corner: *oṃ hrīṃ kumudāya namaḥ*. [Offer this] at the flagpole.
Oṃ agnāvagniḥ. [This is] on the red banner.
Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Śakti. [Offer this] upon the banner. Then, having gone to the southern gate:

Sprinkle the door with water using the sword-mantra: *oṃ akṣarājāya namaḥ*. *oṃ śubhadra kalādvārāya namaḥ*. [Above the door: *te panthāḥ* (RV 10.2.7). *oṃ hrīṃ amodāya namaḥ*. *oṃ hrīṃ pramodāya namaḥ*. [On the two door-posts:]
3a) Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to the auspicious and beautiful archway. [At the archway.]
Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the lotus-eyed one. The flagstaff.

Oṃ hrīṃ aśiyamo r iti || Oṃ hrīṃ daṇḍāya hūṃ phaṭ namaḥ || [Offer this] upon the black banner; having performed the invocation and other rites, and having offered water for the feet, incense, and flowers.
Then, in the southwest corner: Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Vāmana. On the flagstaff:
Oṃ, this is your portion, O Nairṛta! Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to the sword, hūṃ phaṭ!
In the case of the smoke-bannered [deity].
Then, having gone to the western gate, sprinkle it with water while reciting: *oṃ tretāyādi navadarśanariti*.
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Susamākalādārā; [this is for] above the door.
Oṃ, with the mantra "ete panthāḥ," one should worship two jars each.
Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to Jayā. Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to Vijayā.
3b) [The two] branches.
Oṃ hrīḥ, homage to the archway of auspicious liberation. [At the archway.]
Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to Śaṅkhakarṇa. On the flagpole: Oṃ, this has been brought forth, it flows.
Oṃ hrīṃ pāśāya hūṃ phaṭ namaḥ. [This is] for the white banner. Having performed the invocation and other rites, and having offered water for the feet, water for sipping, and flowers.
Having gone to the wind-corner (northwest): *Oṃ hrīṃ sarvanetrāya namaḥ* [at] the flagpole.
Oṃ, that which the wise sages have proclaimed... Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to the Banner (dhvaja), huṃ phaṭ! Namas!
On a green banner.
Then, at the northern gate: sprinkle with the weapon-mantra. Oṃ, salutation to Śuhotra, the door of the Kalās.
Above the door.
"Those paths of yours," so it is said.
Oṃ, homage to the northern archway. [At] the archway.
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Nyāsādāya.
Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Samukha. On the flagstaff: Oṃ agne acchāvarta.
Oṃ hrīṃ gadāya hūṃ phaṭ namaḥ.

Then, having gone to the northeast corner (īśānakona).
Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to the Well-Established One. Banner-pole.
Oṃ, "O you who have been born with a body auspicious and peaceful. Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to the trident, hūṃ phaṭ namaḥ.
On the banner; then again.

Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the Tortoise; in the east.

Thus [are] the deities of the maṇḍala. Milk, curd, ghee, cow urine, and cow dung—one should worship these in succession. One should worship the milk with: *oṃ āpyāyasva*.

Oṃ *janayatu*—thus is the worship. [Offer] divine water and one's own portion. Then, in the southern quarter, one should commence the purification of the ground (*bhūśuddhi*). [Perform] exhalation (*recaka*), inhalation (*pūraka*), and retention (*kumbhaka*). Having worshipped the principles beginning with the Self-principle (*ātmatattva*) up to the Earth-principle (*pṛthvītattva*), one should perform the ritual placement of the principles (*tattvanyāsa*). Thus ends the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*).

Having performed the concluding sacrifice (*antayāga*), one should contemplate oneself as the dual form of Śrīkaṇṭha; through the pacification of the portent, one should bring about auspiciousness with the mantra: *oṃ apahatāḥ suśūrā rakṣaḥ*. Having sipped water (*ācamya*) and performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*), one should sprinkle [the disciple] with all medicinal herbs (*sarvoṣadhīḥ*) while reciting: *āpo asmān mātaraḥ*.
Then, having performed meditative concentration.
5b) Exhalation, inhalation, and retention.

Having performed the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) and the internal sacrifice (antaryāga), having completed the internal sacrifice.
Having washed the special argha vessel, one should worship the vessel.
Parched grain, sandalwood, white mustard seeds, well-prepared unguents, dūrvā grass, kuśa grass, flowers, and sesame seeds.
Thus one should accomplish the eightfold *argha* offering. Thereafter, [the worship] of Śrīkaṇṭha and the others should be performed.
Having fashioned a fragrant maṇḍala upon one's own hand, one should worship Sāga and place it upon the head.
One should contemplate [the deity] as consisting of Viṣṇu; having spontaneously wrapped the head with a turban.
"Oṃ, you are Suparṇa, the Garuḍa. Then, having recited the root mantra of the *ālayāṅga*, one should worship one's own head.
Then one should construct a pavilion in the northeast.

6a) *Oṃ saptayuñjanniri* (etc.). Then, having taken up the sword of knowledge (*jñānakhaḍga*), [performs] the scattering of parched grain (*lājākṣepaṇa*). *Oṃ sarmāsya vadhūtaguṃ rakṣam* (etc.), [this is] the sprinkling (*samājana*). [Then follows] the sprinkling with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*).

Sprinkling with *argha* water; then purification (*samārjana*); then the preparation of the seat: *oṃ hrīṃ anantāya namaḥ*; *oṃ yā idme...*; *oṃ hrīṃ vāsukaye namaḥ*; *oṃ namaste sarpebhyo...*; *oṃ hrīṃ takṣakāya namaḥ*; *oṃ ye vāmī rocane manaso...*

Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Karkoṭaka. Oṃ, that supreme [bond] of Varuṇa. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Padma. Oṃ, through the sacred word (brahman) I approach that truth. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Mahāpadma. Oṃ, those seventy [fetters] of yours, O Varuṇa. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Śaṅkhapāla. Oṃ, you are our [protection], O Agni.
6b) Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Āstīka. Oṃ, [recite] "apasvantaram. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Kulika.

Oṃ, you are the support of the forest. Oṃ Hrīṃ Vauṃ, obeisance to Varuṇa. Oṃ, one should worship me, Varuṇa, starting from the east up to the northeast, including the center. Next follows the worship of the world-protectors (lokapālas); one should worship them below and above.
Oṃ, salutation to the Ṛgveda. Oṃ, I praise Agni, the domestic priest. Then, in the southern direction: Oṃ, for the sake of food, I impel you. Salutation to the Yajurveda. In the west:
Oṃ, salutation to the Sāmaveda. Oṃ, Agni, come for our protection. [The] Northern [direction].
Now, salutation to the Ṛgveda. Oṃ, may the goddesses be for our protection. Oṃ, one should worship the primordial Brahman-knowledge, the first and supreme Brahman.

7a) In the direction of Vāyu (the northwest): Oṃ, homage! One should worship Gaṇapati with "Oṃ namo gaṇebhyaḥ. In the northeast (Īśāna), one should worship the Guru-pitcher (guru-kuṇḍala). One should worship [the lineage] beginning with Śadāśiva and ending with one's own guru.
In the south-eastern direction: one should worship Garuḍa with the mantra "Oṃ śuparṇo 'si garutmān."
Oṃ, one should worship the Viṣṇu-vessel with the Puruṣasūkta mantra.

Oṃ bhīśvate; one should worship the Lakṣmī-kalaśa with this mantra. Oṃ dyauḥ śānti; one should worship the Śānti-kalaśa with this mantra. Oṃ punantu ādityā ṛcā; one should worship the Yajamāna-kalaśa with this verse.

Then, having taken up the *vardhanī* vessel and whirled it around, [he says]: "O Śakra and other gods, you must become the guardians of this water-sacrifice (*jalayāga*) against those who would strike it down. Then, having offered the seat (*āsana*), together with...

One should worship Suśīriṣā with the Puruṣamantra as the increaser of the weapon (*astra*). One should worship the Sword of Knowledge (*jñānakhaḍga*). Oṃ, O Water-born one, you are indeed the form of the line; you are immovable. Accept these thirty swords of knowledge as your own weapon.
You are Viṣṇu in the form of Śakti, and you who bear the embodiment of water;
salutations to you, O Keśava, the cause of grace toward those devoted to you.
O Blessed One, just as this water-pavilion has been constructed with such effort,
so too, O Lord, must this sacrifice— the best of all rites— be protected by you.
Having requested protection.
Oṃ, now, regarding these eight Virūpas, it is obtained that one should worship the Kṣetrapālas.
One should worship the lord of waters with the Vāruṇa hymn.
Then, with "Oṃ, obeisance to the serpents," one should worship the Nāgakuṇḍa.
Then, having gone to the place of the Guru-kalaśa and having propitiated him, one should say: "O, O Blessed One, perform the water-sacrifice (jalayāga); please grant your command."
Then, having performed the water-offering (jalayāga),...
8a) One should purify it by sweeping around like a sacrificial pit:
*Oṃ*, [this is] for Ananta, the western line.

Oṃ, to the lotus on the southern line; Oṃ, likewise to the great lotus on the northern [line]; and to Varuṇa on the central line. Having performed the invocation (āvāhana) and so forth, and having offered water for the feet (pādya) and water for sipping (ācamana), one should then invoke Varuṇa.
One should cause the three channels situated within the self to blaze.
Namely, Iḍā, Piṅgalā, and Suṣumnā.
Having united the Gaṅgā, Yamunā, and Sarasvatī, one should establish the water with the mantra "imaṃ me varuṇa".
Oṃ, the worship [is performed] with the mantra "the immobilization of Varuṇa."
From the east and so forth, [one performs] the consecration of the axle-pen (*akṣavāṭa*). "Oṃ apāśyāgne" for the eastern axle-pen; "Oṃ imam devā" for the southern axle-pen.

8b) "O Waters, today I have entered your words"—with this [verse], the fifth axle-pit is filled. "The divine ones..."—with this, the northern axle-pit is filled. "Become [our] protectors, O heroes"—this is for the fuel-oblation. "O Waters and Plants"—[this is recited] facing the Nāgas.

The ritual procedure: Having offered the Brahmāsana with the mantra "hiranyagarbha," and having filled the Praṇītā vessel with water while reciting "pratyuṣṭam rakṣaḥ," one performs the worship with "āpo hi ṣṭhā" and "idaṃ viṣṇuḥ. [Then follows] "brahmapaktyānam."

The installation of Brahmā; the installation of Viṣṇu with the mantra "viṣṇorarāṭamasi praṇīta"; the worship of the Praṇīta fire with the mantra "trir nipadā vicakrame"; and the worship of the Praṇīta fire dedicated to Brahmā.

9a) Having performed the invocation and so forth, and having offered water for the feet and water for sipping, one should perform the ritual strewing with the mantra "kāriṣiraśiri. Then, according to the form [of the deity], one should place eight jars. One should worship Īśvara with the mantra "triyambakam."

Then, with the mantra "athāśvāgneḥ," one should worship Ananta. One should worship with the *ṛc* verse beginning "oṃ nadībhyaḥ pūjiṣṭham. One should worship two jars each: "oṃ hrīṃ jāhnavyai namaḥ" [to Jāhnavī] and "oṃ yamunāyai namaḥ" [to Yamunā] in the east.
Oṃ hrīṃ, salutations to Godāvarī. Oṃ hrīṃ, salutations to Narmadā. [In the south.]
Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Sindhuve. Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Sarasvatī. [In the] west.
Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Gaṇḍakī. Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Kausikī. In the north.
9b) Then one should worship the Veda-kalaśa; and with the mantra "Oṃ trātāram indram," one should worship Indra.
One should worship Yama with the verse beginning with "yamaṃśuṣe na panthām" and with the mantra.

One should worship the one situated upon the water with the *ṛc* "oṃ tat tvā yāmi. One should worship the Lord of Wealth (*Dhanādhyakṣa*) with the *ṛc* "oṃ vayaṃ soma. One should worship Agni, the consumer of oblations (*Hutāsana*), with "oṃ tvaṃ no agne. One should worship with the *ṛc* "oṃ aśun dhanti. And one should worship Anila with the *ṛc* "oṃ vāto vā."

Oṃ, one should worship Īśāna with the *ṛc* "tamīśānam". One should worship Him who brought this earth, Indra, Brahmā, and Soma, with the *ṛc* "yasminn indraḥ". One should worship Gaṇapati with "namo gaṇebhyaḥ". One should worship the four oceans with the *ṛc* "samudrajyeṣṭhāḥ". One should worship Vāsuki with "varuṇasyottambhanam".
One should worship Soma with the mantra "satvaṃ no agne," and one should worship Takṣaka with the mantra "tat tvā yāmi."
With the mantra "āpo adyānva... one should worship Gāra; with "kāriṣirasi" one should worship Karkoṭaka;
one should worship Varuṇa, Sotambhaṇa, and Ribudha; with "devīḥ" one should worship Padma; and with "āpo hi ṣṭhā" one should worship Bṛhaspati. [One should worship] the divine waters...
One should worship Mahāpadma at Apāṃnyapāśu; one should worship Śukra at Ambhaṃtara; and one should worship Varuṇa and Saṅkhapāla at Ye te.

One should worship Āpo devāḥ, Madhumatīḥ, and Śaṃ no devīr. One should worship Udu tyam, Varuṇa, Pāśaka, and Kulika. Here, the worship of Rāhu consists of "Ye te śatam" and "Varuṇa. May you two be of one mind; salutations to Varuṇa.
Salutations to the serpents; one should worship Ketu. And in the center, [one worships] Varuṇa with "Imam me Varuṇa."
One should worship.

10b) Having performed the invocation (āvāhana), the installation (sthāpana), and offered water for the feet (pādya) and water for sipping (ācamana), one then performs the purification of the vessel (pātra-śodhana) and so forth.
Having performed the purificatory rites beginning with the cutting of the *pavitra*, [one should offer] mental worship to the Lord of Sacrifice (*yajñapati*).

The offering of eighteen fuel-sticks (*samidh-homa*), the purification by sprinkling with water from the supporting vessel (*upayamana*), the worship of the deities beginning with Brahmā, and the worship of the world-protectors (*lokapāla*). Having offered the *pavitra* and the *argha* for Brahmā, [one recites]: "Bhūḥ svāhā! Bhuvaḥ svāhā!"
This [I declare] to you, O Varuṇa, according to the truth, with a sacred prayer—those hundred snares of yours, O Varuṇa, which are directed toward men, O Agni.
O Varuṇa, be most gracious to us; may you be of one mind with us within the waters. Be thou for our sake to Agni.
O King, wide is your depth. [The rites of] impregnation, the male-voice ceremony, the parting of the hair, and the birth-rite.
The naming ceremony.

11a) The ploughing ceremony (hala-prāsana), the first-feeding ceremony (anna-prāsana), the tonsure ceremony (cūḍā-karaṇa), the ear-piercing ceremony (karṇa-bheda), and the vow-binding ceremony (vrata-bandha).
With the *samāvarta* [mantra], there is the union of the falling [of the seed]; this is the *pratiṣṭhā*. One should offer the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) with the root mantra (*mūla*).
Afterwards, one should offer an oblation with sesame seeds.
11b) The establishment of the plow; the vidyās of the pledge.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! O Goddess, these indeed are the sons: Vaṭukanātha, resplendent with a mass of tawny matted hair.
O Three-eyed One, O Flame-mouthed One, accept, accept this offering of perfumes, flowers, and food; destroy, destroy all obstacles!
Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
The offering to the Vaṭukas.

Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! May the Goddess—who is ever pleased by offerings of incense, lamps, and other gifts according to the ritual rules—protect me, whether she resides above the cosmic egg, in the realm of the gods, on the surface of the earth, in the partless state, in the netherworld, in fire, in water, in wind, or wherever she may be situated; whether in a sacred field, a seat, a secondary seat, or in any direction. May she protect me along with her Gurus. Hūṃ Phaṭ! Svāhā!
O Lord of Heroes, worthy of worship by all yogis and all beings, accept, accept this offering!
Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
The Lineage of Yoginīs.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kṣāṃ Kṣīṃ Kṣūṃ Kṣaiṃ Kṣauṃ Kṣaḥ, to your own place,
hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!

Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Geṃ Goṃ Gaḥ! O Gaṇapati, bestower of excellent boons, bring all people under my control; destroy all obstacles; accept, accept this bali-offering accompanied by all desired flavors, svāhā!

12b) Gaṇapati-bali: Thus, the offering of the bali should be made at the previously mentioned locations. The Vaṭuka-bali is offered with the thumb and ring finger; the Yoginī-bali with the index, middle, and ring fingers; and the Kṣetrapāla-bali with the index finger.
The offering to Gaṇapati is for the middle [finger]. The meditation on Vaṭukanātha has been described by the venerable Siddhanātha.

Holding a skull-cup in his hand, adorned with earrings, bearing a staff in his hand, dark blue like fresh darkness, wearing a serpent as his sacred thread, he is the destroyer of obstacles in the worship during the period of the new moon; may Vaṭukanātha, the bestower of success upon those who possess devotion, grant his grace. The Yoginīs, whose forms are at will, hold a noose, a goad, a yoni, a mirror, and a skull-cup.
The bestowal of divinity by the Goddess upon Gaṇanātha, and his state as a divine *liṅga*.
Both [attendants] are red in color; they stand naked, holding a trident, a *ḍamaruka* drum, and a skull-cup.
Five *navavaśalī*, wheat, and so forth, ground into flour and cooked with sugar and ghee, along with red wicks, fragrant substances, and ghee, are placed as lamps upon the *tīrtha*.

13a) Having fashioned a fourfold mandala and established [the image] therein, having washed it with Bhuvaneśvarī and consecrated it with Guhyamālinī, having cast in red gold and other materials, and having knelt upon the ground—
Having invoked Karālī, one should circumambulate three times while reciting the two verses of the *samaya* as follows:
"The inner radiance and the outer radiance, having unified these three channels..."
Having circumambulated the Goddess three times, one should offer the lamp of the lineage (kuladīpa).
O Goddess, Navātmikā, united with all the wheels and their sovereigns;
O Goddess, accept this *ārātrika* for the attainment of the supreme siddhi.
Then, having established the mandala and performed the recitation of the root mantra (mūlavidyā) as many times as possible— counting by the thousands and so forth—
one should offer that recitation with water from the arghya vessel.
"O protector of the most secret of secrets, accept the recitation performed by us;
may there be accomplishment through you. I offer this recitation to you, and one should contemplate that its form as radiant energy has been received by the Supreme Goddess and others."

13b) Then, having taken up the food offering (naivedya), one should provide water for washing the hands. Having prepared scented water (gandhodaka) and offered that garment with the root mantra, one should show a mirror and present a fly-whisk (cāmara).
Again, having worshipped with incense and other offerings, one should display the ten mudrās.
Having offered water from the hollowed palms as a weapon (astra) and mentally assigned oneself along with one's retinue to the Supreme Goddess,
one should repeatedly contemplate oneself as Śrīnātha through prostrations.

Preceded by an act of atonement (*kṣamāpara*), having gone to the ground on one's knees, one should contemplate the Great Wheel (*mahācakra*) as consisting of the secret visualization. One should worship it in those locations with the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*),
as follows:

The Veda-śrī [mantra] is divided into three groups of eight spokes; according to this division, one should worship the Pūrvāmnāya-krama and one's own Samayārcā. With the preceding Śakti, namely *Hsrīṃ Hsrauṃ Suvī*, one should worship the Vāmā-saṃyuta-mala-cakra and so forth, according to their respective divisions.
Having understood the southern *samaya*, one should worship the *rudrārṇa* *samaya*:
Aiṃ Kliṃ E Kliṃ Madadrave Kule Hsrauṃ Rṇṇaṃ Dakṣiṇasamaye Vasurāma.
But that which is without middle, such as the saṃgha and so forth, is distinguished by its divisions.
Having known the final moment, one should worship the thirty-two syllables in sequence.
Hsaiḥ Hsrīṃ Hsrīṃ Hsrphreṃ Hskhphreṃ Bhagavati Aṃbe Hskṣmlvryīṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ Kubjike Hskhphreṃ Hskhphrīṃ Hskhphruṃ Ghore Aghore Aghorāmukhi Cchāṃ Cchīṃ Kiṇi Kiṇi Vicce Hrīṃ Hskhphreṃ Hsrīṃ Hsphrīṃ.
Hsrīṃ! This is the Mistress of the West, the thirty-two-syllable Samaya-vidyā.

Having understood the equal [vowel] and the curved [consonant] with its moments (*kṣaṇa*), as well as the subsequent [syllables], one should emit those very [syllables] which are the seventeen parts (*kalā*) of the phoneme-convention (*varṇasamaya*). *Khphreṃ* Mahācaṇḍayogeśvari! This is the nine-syllable mantra of the subsequent convention (*uttarasamayavidyā*). *Ma ekhapharamahā ca na ḍaya eṣa savari*: this is the seventeen-part [mantra].

Having contemplated the one who brings about the devouring of time, whose nature consists of the manifestation of the primordial rays of the great *rāga-yāga*, and having worshipped her with the *samaya-mantras* from that [state],

Just as one should worship the Vedas, the Āśramas, and the Buddhist divisions— knowing them to be variations endowed with the syllables of the *argha* offering— in the same way, one should worship [the Buddha] with the vajras and so forth that have descended from the cloudless sky.

*Oṃ tore tutāre ture svāhā*. This is the *Tārā-mantra* according to the Buddhist tradition. Having understood that the Vaiṣṇava [mandala] consists of sixteen spokes (dviraṣṭāra) and the appearance of a pedestal (*vedikā*), one should not worship with the mantra beginning with *veda* (the four-syllable *oṃ*). Having understood that the Vaiṣṇava [mandala] consists of eight petals and an inner eight-spoked [circle], one should not worship with the eight-syllable mantra: *Oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya oṃ*.
Having understood the Śākta view of the central triangle (*triśṛṅgāṭa*), one should worship with the *vāgbhava* [syllable].

Then, having offered a handful of flowers once each to the goddesses beginning with Kāmeśvarī there with the *samaya-vidyā*, one should [worship] the goddess situated in the center with the *samaya-vidyā*.
Having offered a flower: therein, Kāmeśvarī, Cakreśvarī, and Bhagamālinī are the Samaya-vidyās. To the east, when held, [is]:
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ * *? Trayāṃ Rāṃ Lāṃ Vāṃ Sāṃ, O bestower of the fruits of desire and will, O innate subduer of all beings!
15a) Kṣobhakari hūṃ 3 aiṃ drāṃ drīṃ klīṃ vlūṃ saḥ aiṃ, obeisance to Tripurākāmeśvarī.
Kāmeśvarī is the Samaya-vidyā.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! O accomplisher of all tasks, Vajreśvarī, situated within the diamond cage, Hrīṃ Kline Aiṃ Kroṃ! O you who are eternally flowing with intoxication, Hrīṃ! Salutation to Vajrānandā.
Thus ends the Samaya-vidyā of Vajreśvarī.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aiṃ! O Bhagabhuge, O Bhagini, O Bhagodari, O Bhagamāle, O Bhagavāhe,

O Bhagaguhye, O Bhagayoni, O Bhaganipātani, O Sarvabhagavaśaṅkari, O Bhagarūpe, O Nityaklinne, O Bhagasvarūpe, O you who bring all bhagas under your control, O Giver of Boons, O you whose semen is heroic, O Bhagaklinne, Kliṃ!
O Dravā, moisten; O Amoghe Bhagavicce, cause to flow; O Kṣubha, agitate all beings;
O Bhageśvarī, aiṃ vluṃ jaṃ vlūṃ bheṃ vlūṃ moṃ vlūṃ heṃ vlūṃ aiṃ, make all the bhagas moist!
15b) Bhāvagamānaya strīṃ hara vlūṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Bhagamālinī.
Bhagamālinī is the vidyā of the samaya.
O Śrī Bhagavatī, Nityākāmeśvarī, you who bring all beings under your power, O Tripurabhairavī, Aiṃ Vicce Hrīṃ, obeisance to Mahātripuraśundarī!
The root goddess is the vidyā of the samaya.
Then, having gratified the two Supreme Lords with circumambulations and prostrations, and having offered the *arghya* for the withdrawal (*parāṅmukha-arghya*) to the host of attendant deities,
one should take the Goddess from the seat of *kuśa* grass within the mandala by means of the *saṃhāra-mudrā*, [placing her] within the great lotus forest.

Having drunk the interior of the triangle (*śṛṅgāṭodara*), through the distinction between the external and internal, one should contemplate the *kāmakalā* and conceive it as the *bindu*. As stated in the *Ādiśruta*:
"The *khecarīmudrā*, together with the *vardhana*, brings about the dissolution of the mind."
Until then, one should remain in the state of *unmanī* at the junction (*śṛṅgāṭa*). As it is said in the *Śukrastotra*:
"The sprout of consciousness (*vid-aṅkura*) and the forms of the *kāmakalās*—the two [aspects] of the *bindu* are to be meditated upon as immeasurable splendor;
by means of this, the two unstruck sounds (*anāhatadhvani*) abide in the wheel."
In the interval between births.
16a) Having properly dissolved the two drops (bindu) in the form of the moon and sun situated upon its support, flowing from the pair of sides,
as well as the portion at the tip of the flame of fire below that, which has the shape of a line (rekhā);
Then, having accepted the grace by means of the root-mantra with the three seed-syllables at the end of the three principles (tattvas) and ending with "svāhā."

One should worship Kumārī and Vaṭuka. *Hrīṃ* is the mantra of Kumārī; *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ* is the mantra of Vaṭuka. Having prepared a mandala consisting of a triangle, a circle, and a square in front of Kumārī and Vaṭuka, one should worship the mandala—which is permeated by the six vowels and the syllable *hrīṃ*—and [place] the self-supporting vessel (*svādhāra*).

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the *svaśvamantra* and having cast a drop (*bindu*) from the special offering water (*viśeṣārgha*), one should worship her with devotion through gold, garments, fragrant flowers, betel, and other such items; with various kinds of foods to be chewed, sucked, and licked;
with ointments and the like; with varieties of honey and wine; and with lamps.
Having offered the *arghya* and performed the salutation at the feet, one should prepare three vessels; [the number of] Cakra-deities may be sixty-four,
or thirty-two,
or down to four.
16b) Having performed the ritual installation preceded by washing the feet and offering water for honor (*arghya*) according to one's ability,
and having constantly worshipped the wheel of the Yoginīs— which is free from deceit and guile— within the reality (*tattva*), [one should offer] the three vessels.
Having caused [the rite] to be performed, and having prayed with devotion to the Supreme Goddess, one should then, by her permission, [recite] the three seed-syllables of the Root-Vidyā,

the fourth seed-syllable, and the fourfold "tapastinva," ending with *svāhā*. Preceded by meditation on the Guru, one should eternally arouse the Śakti with a state of non-dual absorption (*asamaraśa-bhāva*) for the sake of attaining that [state].
Having offered oblations into the four vessels, and having displayed the outer *bali* while keeping the command (*ājñā*) of the Śrīcakra foremost,

one should consume the vessel of the *samaya*. Having personally partaken of all the offerings, such as the food (*naivedya*), and having given the remainder to the fellow practitioners of the *samaya*, that very prasāda—

17a) The worship of those practitioners is described as it truly is. As follows: In the place of one's own crest-jewel (ala), there is no ritual action or recitation for Gaṇeśa and Vaṭuka; rather, they are to be fully worshipped through recitations in the form of intuitive inspiration (*pratibhā*) according to their respective mantras.

Having recollected the mantra of thirty-two syllables— the supreme *kalā* which is the witness of the cessation of the great delusion of both difference and non-difference at the *dvādaśānta*, and which sustains the universe as the protector of the *kula-kṣetra* below one's own *mūlādhāra*— and having recollected that which is beyond all states, beginning with "all that is manifest and deeply asleep," etc.

Having meditated upon the commitment (samaya) of the sixty-four Yoginīs, divided into [sixty-four] parts from the head down to the secret place by means of the previously indicated mantra; and having recollected the lineage of gurus (gurukrama), which consists of the intellect, vital breath, objects, and the self, in the form of a garland of qualities, starting from the northwest (īśāna) up to the southeast (cora) within the square and sixteen-petaled lotuses in one's own left side.

Having placed the sixfold seat, which is the sixth form, upon the head, forehead, between the eyebrows, the uvula, throat, heart, navel, genitals, and the foundation (ādhāra), one should contemplate the wheel of the mind located at the *śṛṅgāṭa* of the *kula*.

Having invoked the Vāhanavidyā from the three-fold Kulāyā within the lotus of the Kūrma [cakra], while recollecting it, one should bring about the state of *samarasīkaraṇa* (equilibrium). When [the energy] has become unified within the Aparakuṇḍalinī, one should contemplate the eight supernatural powers (*aṇimā* etc.
in the cardinal and intermediate directions, extending from the crown of the head (*cūḍā*) through the divine pervasion (*vyāpti*) to the four squares situated at the top of the head.

Then, one should worship the ten mudrās beginning with Brahmā within the inner triangle in the manner previously described. Having worshipped them in a clockwise direction in the form of a mass of rays like rubies, one should then recollect the Mistress of the Wheel, Tripurā, who is the eternal [deity] of the six limbs and the pride of the wheel. There, by that...
Having performed the offering with the mantra and recalled the drinking of the supreme nectar-portion (*parāmṛtakalā*),

one should visualize, right there within the four-petaled lotus, a cluster of rays from the sixteen digits (*kalā*) starting from the tip of the forehead, revolving counter-clockwise; and [visualize] the Mistress of that Wheel, Tripureśvarī, and Nityā as before.
Then, having recollected the one who pervades the wheel (*cakravyāpinī*), and having offered [it] there,
having performed the supreme touch (*paramārśa*) of the sacrificial vessel (*satra*), in the interval between those, right there among these—

Having visualized a lotus with eight petals resembling rubies, one should remember the previously mentioned cluster of eight rays beginning with Anaṅga located within the forehead in the cardinal and intermediate directions starting from the southeast. Then,
having offered that to the Mistress of the Wheel, the eternal Tripurasundarī, and having remembered the mantra:

Having entered the pure wheel (*śucicakra*) in the center of the *bindu*, the fourteen goddesses offer that wheel to its mistress (*cakreśvarī*). Then, having performed [the offering] starting from the back with a counter-clockwise rotation (*vāmāvarta*) as before, one performs the ten pairs in the *laṃvikā* and the throat; likewise in the heart-lotus, in the eight wheels.

From that point, one should worship the eight Vasini goddesses by circling counter-clockwise. Having offered them to the Mistress of that Cakra (Cakreśvarī) and having remembered her with the mantra, one should then remember the triad of goddesses beginning with Kāmeśvarī— starting from the front in the triangle of the Nābhi-cakra— and having offered them to the Mistress of that Cakra while circling clockwise, the offering is performed with the mantra.

Having remembered the Mistress of that Wheel (taccakreśvarī) within the Kulakuṇḍalī by means of the root mantra (mūlavidyā) and the mantra of all the protective seats (pādupapīṭha) in the holder of the mudrā (18b).

Just as one might remember a form and, having sipped water from the hollow of one's cupped hands, offer it; then, without reciting the mantra, one offers worship by meditating upon the eighty million pores of the body. One should meditate on sixty-four hundred thousand million great yoginīs, each residing within a single pore, flowing with nectar from the *śṛṅgāṭa*.

Having performed worship with the mantra "I worship the Śrīpādukā," [one worships] the eight locations: the Mūlādhāra, Svādhiṣṭhāna, Maṇipūraka, Anāhata, Kaṇṭha, Laṃbikā, Nose, and the auspicious space between the eyebrows.

Beginning from the center of the brows (bhrūmadhya), having worshipped each one individually with perfumes up to the twelfth [digit] of the eight eternal goddesses (nityāṣṭaka) ending with Vasiṣṭhā; having recollected there the Supreme Gaurī-vidyā which carries the supreme nectar, as well as the Samaya-vidyā which carries the supreme nectar; and the five powers (śaktipañcaka) and the four fires.
19a) By means of the state of being both the one who drives away and the one driven away by [the rays], his own body— [which is] in the form of the ocean of those [rays]—
is like a ruby through the digit of nectar of the Makula-flower, and like ten million moons through the coolness of the moonlight.
O Adhvaryu, having placed within that heart of supreme nectar—

[which is] permeated by the practice of the power of reflective awareness (*vimarśaśakti*)— the seed-syllable consisting of the form of the first letter, and having remained established in the nature of the experience of supreme bliss, [one attains] the earthly [element].

May the entirety of the fragrance of virtues be offered in the form of flowers and incense; may even the subtle essence of virtue be offered as a radiant garland of lamps and as camphor-illumination at night.
Having offered the food, beginning with the fragrant substances, to the devourers who are equal to all the gods without exception;
having performed circumambulation and prostration, which constitute the bodily activity characterized by the quality of the wind element (*vāyu-tattva*);

and having arranged the musical instruments and auspicious recitations, which are the sound characterized by the quality of the space element (*ākāśa-tattva*); [she whose] form is the delusion of the intellect...
Having conceptualized the functions [of the senses] ending with the mind, intellect, and ego— [which are like] tethered animals—
the knowledge that arises from the stream of hearing regarding those [functions] is then manifold.
Having gratified the Supreme Sovereigns, and having offered the casting away of the impurities of *mala*, *māyā*, and *karman* by means of the sword of knowledge (*jñānakhaḍga*),

one should present to the Goddesses an uninterrupted stream of wine flowing from the interior of the skull and the *śṛṅgāṭa* (triangle), and [one should offer it] oneself through the power of reflective awareness (*vimarśaśakti*).

Having proceeded with the offering of the *śṛṅgāṭaka* (the triangular vessel) and so forth, one should become filled with bliss (*nandamaya*), characterized by the state of the reality that moves within the mind—the worship consisting of the state of flavor-union (*samarasībhāva*) in the supreme non-dual state. Then, one should perform the rinsing of the mouth (*ācamanīya*) and the offering of betel leaf mixed with camphor using the root mantra; this is the intermediate worship (*antarapūjā*). Thereafter, [that which is] to be described...
One should perform the placement of the wheels (cakranyāsa).
The Lord said:
O beloved, hear now the mantra-purification and the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the wheel.
Homage to the venerable gurus!
Jayā, Vijayā, Jayantī, Aparājitā,
Nandā, Bhadrā, Bhīmā, and likewise the eight Kalās.
Divya-yoginī, Mahā-yoginī, Siddhi-yoginī, Gaṇeśvarī, Sākinī,
Kālarātrī, Ūrdhvakeśī, and Niśākarī.
Deep and not coarse due to its roar.
Pavanā, Gītalolikā, Bhīṣaṇā, Mahānandā, and likewise Jvālāmukhī;
Piśācī, Hastinī, Jakṣaṇī, and likewise Dhūrjaṭī.
Viṣabhakṣasarvaśiddhi, Tuṣṭi, and likewise Icchā; Mātaṃbhaṣī, Kākadṛṣṭi, and likewise Ālipurāntakī.
The Rākṣasī of terrible roar, red-eyed, possessing every form,
the terrifying one, fierce and wrathful, the paralyzer, and the devourer of men.
20b) Nārabhadra, Mahākālī, Kaṅkālī, Vikṛtānanā, Krodhalī, Bhīmabhadra, Vāyuvegā, and Bhayānanā.
Brāhmī, Vaiṣṇavī, Raudrī, Carcikā, and likewise Īśvarī;
Vārāhī, Nārasimhī, and the fourfold Śivādyutī.
O Age-less One, O Great Yoginī, always accept my offering!
Aiṃ 5! [Accept] all the pīṭhas, upapīṭhas, and so forth, as well as the gates and sub-gates.
The fields, sub-fields, and assemblies are situated, illuminating all directions;
they exist within the great netherworlds, the cosmic egg, and in the supreme interior of all places.
The yoginīs, the heroes, and the lords of heroes have all come to that very place;
O Śrīnātha, bestower of boons, may this great wheel be mine.
O Goddess, for those who with devotion serve the teachings and are intent upon the worship and honor of the Guru,
may you always grant them the grace of all spiritual attainments.
O Goddess, those on the surface of the earth who bear malice toward the heroes and yoginīs—
[offer] the bali-oblation at the assembly of the conduct of the samaya.
His vision, consisting of the Śruti and Smṛti, drew away the flesh, fat,
and bone that sustained life within the bodies of wicked Yoginīs.
The venerable Oṃkāra is proclaimed as the Pīṭha, together with Abhayā;
the Upapīṭhas, however, are located in the cardinal directions, the intermediate directions, and the various [other] regions.
The earth, the netherworld, and the cosmic egg— within all these places and beyond them—
the Yoginī, whose self is united with Yoga, remains according to the established rule.

In the sequences of the heroes (*vīrakrama*), the lords of heroes (*vīrendra*) are the practitioners (*sādhaka*); in the sequences of attainment (*siddhikrama*), the sons of attainment (*siddhiputraka*) and the masters (*ācārya*) are the virtuous ones who have briefly summarized the observances (*samaya*).
Whether in a city or a separate village, on a mountain or by a great river, at a pond, a well, or a forest, or in a cemetery or a circle of mothers.
Yogis who assume various forms, diverse and manifold—
may they all be satisfied and always accept this offering.
I have come to you for refuge; I shall bestow all their fruits.
Whatever sequence of actions I shall perform during this present life, and whatever ritual I shall carry out, it shall be through the offering of oblations and flowers.

May the one who bestows contentment through giving, the contemplator of all things, grant success for the pacification of all defects; may the power of Śiva be pleased within my womb eternally. Aiṃ 5.
The offering for the Yoginīs.

Aiṃ 5! May there be perfect satisfaction for all beings—those of various forms existing in the earth, the atmosphere, and the netherworld; those dwelling in the cardinal and intermediate directions; and those eternal, divine beings. Svāhā! Bhūta-bali. Aiṃ 5 Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Ha Hauṃ Haṃ Haḥ Oṃ.

O you of great strength and prowess, radiant with the mass of matted hair of Kapila, three-eyed one with flaming mouths, accept this offering of incense, perfume, lamps, and oblations! Roar in the form of Bhairava! *turu turu*, *la la*, *kha kha*, *he he*!
Accept this offering and worship for the Lord of the Great Ḍāmaras! May there be success! *Svāhā!*
The offering to Bhairava.
